prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an outdoor yard layout where a brick building wall with recessed windows and a black ground box (~1.5–2 m away) bounds the left, a grassy lawn stretches forward, and trees and a white minivan sit in the far right background (>8–10 m away, dark). In the lower foreground within arm's reach (~0.4–1.0 m, brightest white), a small child stands inside or beside a rectangular plastic tub while a white cloth at the bottom-left and the camera wearer's hand holding a blue bowl/scoop at the bottom-right (frame 5) enter closer to the lens (~0.3–0.5 m). Across the 5 frames, the camera tilts slightly left and downward while the child shifts from the bottom-center inside the tub (facing away/left in frame 1, dipping mostly out of view in frames 2–3) to standing to the right of the tub in frames 4–5 (~0.7–1.0 m away, ~0.2 m from the tub rim) facing away and toward the building while the wearer's hand and bowl partially occlude the child's lower right side in frame 5. The depth map makes the continuous ground-plane gradient, the recessed depth of the window frames, and the sharp foreground separation between the child's head/shoulders and the lawn behind them much clearer than RGB alone. However, it is unreliable inside the saturated white foreground where the child's head, the tub rim, and the overlapping hand/bowl in frame 5 lose internal depth contrast, and on the reflective glass windows which appear artificially deeper than the surrounding brick wall.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground and background objects against a black background, detecting the child ('person') at the bottom (~0.5–1.0 m away) and the white minivan ('car') on the right (>10 m away, ~9–10 m behind the child), plus the camera wearer's hand ('person') and blue plastic container ('frisbee') at ~0.3–0.5 m in the bottom-right of frame 5. In frames 1–2, only the child's head and right hand gripping the tub rim are visible at the bottom-left and bottom-center while the minivan is partially cropped at the right edge; in frame 3 the child's head drops low enough to be missed entirely, and in frames 4–5 the child rises into view on the right of the tub with their back turned toward the camera wearer while the wearer's hand and blue container enter from the lower right and partially occlude the child's right arm and torso. This map clearly tracks the small, partially cropped background car at the far right edge of frames 3–4 and separates the overlapping wearer's hand, blue container, and child in frame 5, which blend together at the frame boundary in RGB. However, the segmentation is highly unreliable in several places: it completely misses the plastic tub, white cloth, black utility box, and building in all frames, fails to detect the child's head in frame 3, mislabels the blue bowl/scoop as a 'frisbee' in frame 5, and hallucinates a lime-green 'person' mask over the background trees and grass in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only a single detection in frame 1 at the bottom-left (~0.5–0.8 m away, within arm's reach of the camera wearer and the tub rim) and is completely black across frames 2–5. In frame 1, a compact cluster of yellow body keypoints marks the child's head/neck orientation (facing away and slightly right toward the lawn, not looking at the camera wearer) and a magenta hand skeleton marks the child's right hand gripping the top edge of the plastic tub just to the right of and slightly below their head (~0.15 m apart), while their torso and legs are occluded by the tub and lower frame boundary. This skeletal overlay pinpoints the exact finger joint configuration of the child's right hand on the tub rim and confirms the head orientation in frame 1 more explicitly than the blurred RGB head alone. However, the pose map is extremely unreliable across the sequence, failing to detect the child's head in frames 2–3, completely missing the child's clearly visible head, back, shoulders, and left arm in frames 4–5 as they move to the right of the tub, and missing the camera wearer's right hand entering at the bottom-right of frame 5.
